name: Asaph
overview: Asaph was a prominent Levite musician and worship leader appointed by King David to lead temple music, specifically playing cymbals in the tabernacle service, as seen in Ezra 3:10 and Nehemiah 12:46. He was also the father of Joah and a descendant of Kohath, with his family continuing the sacred role of temple singers after the exile, evidenced by the recorded numbers of his descendants in Ezra 2:41 and Nehemiah 7:44. Additionally, Asaph held responsibilities beyond music, serving as the keeper of the king's forest to supply timber for the temple and city walls, as noted in Nehemiah 2:8. His descendants maintained oversight of temple worship and the house of God, highlighting a lasting legacy of faithful service in worship and practical support for God's house.
